record.paper_title: Semantic Subtyping: Challenges, Perspectives, and Open Problems
record.context_brief: Nature and limits of semantic subtyping
record.original_question: Is semantic subtyping merely an alternative semantic route to type systems that could in principle also be axiomatized syntactically, or does it fundamentally yield genuinely new classes of type systems? Equivalently, what are the real limits and degrees of freedom of the semantic-subtyping approach, and to what extent can the extensional interpretation underlying the models be systematized and characterized?

evidence.quote: As a matter of facts, we do not know whether the semantic subtyping approach is an innovative approach that yields to the definition of brand new type systems or it is just a new way to define old systems (or rather, systems that could be also defined in the good old syntactic way).
A more technical point is to investigate whether and to which extent it is possible to systematise the definition of the extensional interpretation.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Background. In the design of typed programming languages, a subtyping relation between types is traditionally defined syntactically by a deductive system: one fixes a grammar of types (typically with constructors such as products, arrows, recursive types, and possibly Boolean combinators ∨, ∧, ¬) and gives a set of inference rules deriving judgements t ≤ s. The "semantic subtyping" approach instead proceeds as follows. One fixes a class of models in which every type t is mapped to a subset ⟦t⟧ of some domain D (an "extensional interpretation"), required to commute with the Boolean type connectives in the set-theoretic way (⟦t∨s⟧ = ⟦t⟧∪⟦s⟧, ⟦¬t⟧ = D∖⟦t⟧, etc.) and to interpret each non-Boolean type constructor in a way faithful to its operational meaning. Subtyping is then defined extensionally by

  t ≤ s  ⇔  ⟦t⟧ ⊆ ⟦s⟧  in every such model.

Problem. Address the following two interrelated questions about the expressive power and structure of this approach.

(a) Determine whether the semantic-subtyping methodology is essentially a different presentation of subtyping relations that could equivalently be obtained by a syntactic deductive system, or whether it produces type systems whose subtyping relations cannot be captured by any reasonable finite syntactic axiomatization. More precisely, give either:
  (i) a general theorem showing that for every type system arising from a semantic-subtyping construction (in a suitably formalized class) there exists an equivalent finitely axiomatized syntactic subtyping system; or
  (ii) an explicit example of a type system definable by semantic subtyping whose induced subtyping relation provably admits no such syntactic axiomatization, together with a characterization of the obstruction.

(b) Provide a systematic theory of the extensional interpretation. That is, formalize a general framework that takes as input a signature of type constructors together with their intended operational behavior and outputs a canonical extensional interpretation ⟦·⟧ together with sufficient conditions ensuring (1) soundness with respect to the operational semantics, (2) decidability of the induced subtyping relation, and (3) uniqueness or canonicity of the resulting interpretation. Identify the precise degrees of freedom (parameters, choices) available in the construction of such interpretations and characterize the boundary cases where the method fails or yields non-canonical alternatives.
artifact.status_search_result: The two questions—whether semantic subtyping yields genuinely new type systems versus alternatives to syntactically axiomatizable ones, and whether the definition of the extensional interpretation can be systematized—are stated as open problems in the semantic-subtyping literature. Subsequent work (e.g., extensions to the π-calculus, objects and classes, SMT-based decision procedures, logical approaches) has applied the methodology to new settings but, to the best of available public evidence, has not produced a general meta-theorem either equating semantic subtyping with syntactic axiomatizations or systematically characterizing all admissible extensional interpretations. Status appears still open.

status_evidence.title: Semantic Subtyping: Challenges, Perspectives, and Open Problems
status_evidence.snippet: we do not know whether the semantic subtyping approach is an innovative approach that yields to the definition of brand new type systems or it is just a new way to define old systems
status_evidence.claim: The questions are explicitly posed as open.

status_evidence.title: Semantic Subtyping for Objects and Classes
status_evidence.snippet: Applies the semantic-subtyping methodology to a new setting (objects and classes) without giving a general systematization theorem.
status_evidence.claim: Subsequent work extends the method case-by-case rather than providing a unifying meta-theory.

status_evidence.title: A Logical Approach to Deciding Semantic Subtyping
status_evidence.snippet: Provides decision procedures for specific semantic-subtyping instances via logic, but does not characterize the limits of the approach in general.
status_evidence.claim: Decision-procedure work does not resolve the meta-questions about expressive limits.
